title: Helmsman Taskizer: interactive runbook snapshotting and safe replay
creator: Ava Park
description: Background: On-call and support teams frequently run multi-step remediation runbooks that combine CLI steps, console actions and API calls. Current runbooks are brittle to interruption and lack a concise snapshot format for safe replay or dry-run in a sandbox. Goal: Create a lightweight 'Helmsman Taskizer' service that converts interactive runbook executions into idempotent task snapshots, stores them with audit metadata, and provides a safe replay/dry-run path in an isolated sandbox. Success criteria: 1) single-button snapshot export for any runbook execution (CLI/Console) with metadata, 2) ability to replay a snapshot in a read-only dry-run mode that reports side-effect predictions, 3) safe replay mode that enforces RBAC/approvals and prevents escalation unless explicitly approved, 4) end-to-end telemetry (per-step latency, success/failure, toggled flags) surfaced in Console. Out of scope: full automated remediation engine, long-running orchestration across external customer accounts, multi-tenant snapshot sharing. Technical approach: instrument runbook runner to emit a canonical step sequence (idempotency tokens, input refs, expected side-effects). Persist snapshots to object storage with HMAC signing and optional KMS encryption. Provide a replay sandbox service that can simulate API calls against a mock backend or replay against a mirrored staging environment depending on mode. Add a small web UI in Console to browse snapshots, request approvals, and trigger replays. Integrations: link snapshots to Incident and Ticket IDs, attach to audit logs, surface in on-call workflow. Rollout: alpha to SRE and internal support team -> gated beta with canary approval flow -> org-wide opt-in. Risks: storing snapshots contains sensitive context; require redaction rules and KMS keys per-org. Complex external system interactions may make dry-run predictions incomplete. Monitoring and rollback: snapshot-to-replay ratio, replay failure rate, time-to-approval SLA, and unauthorized replay attempts will be tracked. Implementation phases: spike (POC snapshot format + minimal replay simulator), core (storage, signing, replay modes, RBAC), UX (console browse + approvals), telemetry + SLOs, docs + runbook migration guides.
comments: 2026-02-22: Spike complete — PoC creates JSON snapshot from runbook runner with step hashes and idempotency tokens. PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood/ops-helmsman/pull/11
2026-02-25: Design review with SRE and Support. Decided on two replay modes: dry-run (no external writes) and gated-live (requires approval). Action: define HMAC envelope format and redaction policy.

2026-03-02: Security flagged need for KMS-wrapped snapshot encryption for anything containing credentials. Added redaction and tokenization step to pipeline. Security ticket: https://confluence.redwood.io/display/SEC/Helmsman+Snapshot+Security
2026-03-05: End-to-end demo to PM and Support. Feedback: include predicted side-effects table and explicit confirmation step before any live replay. Added telemetry hooks for per-step durations.

2026-03-10: Implementation note — using S3 bucket 'ops-snapshots-prod' with key prefix helmsman/{org}/{yyyy}/{id}. Retention policy 90 days by default; infra will provide TTL lifecycle. TODO: add per-org retention override UI.
2026-03-12: PR opened for core API and storage: https://github.com/redwood/ops-helmsman/pull/1423. Initial e2e tests added. QA: need simulated failure injection for replay safety tests.
